title: Noah Smith and Azeem Azhar discuss the AI boom
gist: Very thin podcast announcement: Noah Smith and Azeem Azhar (Exponential View) discuss the AI boom and the possibility of an AI bust, prompted by Smith's Oct 15 post 'AI vs. the railroads'; Smith says they reached no firm conclusions. The page body is almost entirely reader comments, which are not used as author claims.

insights.claim: Noah Smith and Azeem Azhar of Exponential View held a podcast discussion on the AI boom and the possibility of an AI bust.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Signals that the risk of an AI investment bust is a live topic among prominent tech-economics commentators.
insights.quote: talk to him about the AI boom, and the possibility of an AI bust

insights.claim: Smith's framing of the AI investment cycle draws on a historical analogy to the railroads, from his earlier post 'AI vs. the railroads'.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The railroad analogy implies a possible overbuild-then-bust capex cycle; useful lens for AI infrastructure exposure.

insights.claim: Noah Smith says he and Azeem Azhar reached no firm conclusions on whether the AI boom will end in a bust.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: No directional call here; treat as uncertainty rather than a bust or boom signal.
insights.quote: I don’t think we reached any firm conclusions
